extracted.intended_audience: scholars and researchers in public administration, algorithmic governance, and human–AI decision-making (also policymakers and experimental social scientists)
extracted.subtask_description: Designing and conducting vignette-based survey experiments to test how human decision-makers in public-sector settings respond to algorithmic versus human expert advice, with focus on automation bias and selective adherence. Includes methodological choices for stimuli, randomization, preregistration, and sample selection/replication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Automation bias (definition and test)
rubrics_metrics.description: Automation bias: undue deference to automated systems by human actors that disregard contradictory information from other sources or do not thoroughly search for additional information—i.e., use of automation as a heuristic replacement for vigilant information seeking and processing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To test automation bias, compare adherence to an algorithmic prediction versus an equivalent human-expert prediction when both are confronted with contradictory external evidence (supplement algorithmic advice with additional inputs that conflict with the automated recommendation). Hypothesis stated as: 'Decision-makers are more likely to trust and to follow algorithmic advice than human advice, when faced with similar contradicting external evidence.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Selective adherence (definition and test)
rubrics_metrics.description: Selective adherence: propensity to adopt advice selectively when it matches pre-existing stereotypes about decision subjects (assigning greater weight to stereotype-congruent information and contesting inputs that contradict them).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Test whether participants are more likely to follow advice (human or algorithmic) that matches stereotypical views of the decision subject by experimentally manipulating the target's group background (e.g., ethnic minority vs majority) and measuring adherence. Hypothesized as: 'Decision-makers are more likely to follow advice that matches stereotypical views of the decision subjects.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Exacerbated selective adherence (algorithm amplification)
rubrics_metrics.description: Theorized mechanism that algorithms may amplify selective adherence because algorithmic outputs can act as a 'moral buffer' and provide a seemingly neutral endorsement of biased decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Test whether selective adherence is stronger when advice is algorithmic versus human by interacting advice source with stereotype-alignment. Hypothesized as: 'Selective adherence is likely to be exacerbated when decision-makers receive an algorithmic rather than a human advice.' Consider psychological distancing, reduced sense of responsibility, and algorithms giving 'permission' to act on latent biases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriate counterfactual for algorithm effects
rubrics_metrics.description: To isolate algorithm-specific effects, the relevant comparator should be an equivalent numeric advice produced by a human expert rather than a no-advice condition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design conditions where the numeric output format is the same across algorithmic and human-expert conditions (e.g., both present a 1–10 predictive score) to avoid conflating algorithm effects with presence/absence of advice or numeric format differences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include contradictory external evidence to diagnose automation bias
rubrics_metrics.description: Automation bias can be effectively tested only when algorithmic advice is supplemented with additional inputs that contradict it, forcing decision-makers to choose which cue to follow.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Present participants with at least two inputs (e.g., a numeric prediction and a qualitative evaluation) that are deliberately incongruent; vary level of incongruence (high vs modest) to test robustness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vignette-based bureaucratic decision task design
rubrics_metrics.description: Use realistic public-sector vignette tasks (e.g., school-board personnel decisions) where lay persons or civil servants plausibly act as decision-makers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select tasks that map onto real bureaucratic roles to enhance external validity, and consider replicating with both citizen samples and actual civil servants to generalize findings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Randomization of experimental conditions and stimuli order
rubrics_metrics.description: Random assignment to main conditions (algorithmic vs human expert) and to other treatment variations (e.g., distribution of scores across targets, level of incongruence).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Randomize order of targets and randomize assignment of ILE scores (4, 6, 8) across teachers to avoid order effects and idiosyncratic confounds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Present both quantitative and qualitative inputs
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide participants with two data inputs per decision subject: one qualitative summary (e.g., HR evaluation) and one numeric prediction score (e.g., 1–10).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure formats are realistic and comparable to real-world tools (the article used an ILE score designed to resemble COMPAS). Keep qualitative inputs standardized and vary only as intended by treatment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primary outcome coding (follow algorithmic score)
rubrics_metrics.description: Main outcome is participants' likelihood to follow the numeric score (ILE) operationalized as a binary choice: coded 1 if participant chooses to fire the teacher with the lowest ILE score, 0 otherwise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Predefine dichotomous outcome and use appropriate statistical models (e.g., logistic regression) to compare rates across conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-registration and power analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: Preregister study design and analysis plan and conduct power calculations to determine detectable effect sizes (example: estimated OR = 1.5 detectable with power 0.8).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide preregistration link and justify sample sizes based on anticipated effect sizes and desired power; report any deviations transparently.

rubrics_metrics.name: Participant inclusion/exclusion criteria and attention checks
rubrics_metrics.description: Exclude participants failing attention checks or completing the survey implausibly quickly; for selective adherence analyses, exclude participants not of target demographic (e.g., not of Dutch descent).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pre-specify attention checks and minimum completion time thresholds (the study excluded those completing in less than 3 minutes) and report exclusion counts and rationale.

rubrics_metrics.name: Replication across samples and attention to contemporaneous events
rubrics_metrics.description: Replicate experiments across multiple samples (e.g., two citizen samples and one sample of civil servants) and interpret findings in light of contemporaneous real-world events (e.g., childcare benefits scandal) that may affect responses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use replication to test robustness and consider contextual moderators (heightened awareness due to scandals may attenuate biases).

rubrics_metrics.name: Manipulation credibility and framing
rubrics_metrics.description: Bolster credibility of the predictive score by providing participants with efficacy information (e.g., 'has proven highly effective… 95% accuracy') consistently across advice-source conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Frame information equivalently across conditions so that perceived reliability does not vary by treatment except for the intended source manipulation (algorithm vs human).

rubrics_metrics.name: Control stimulus attributes to minimize confounds
rubrics_metrics.description: Standardize irrelevant attributes of vignette targets—e.g., all teachers female, typical Dutch names, same subject area—to prevent extraneous variation influencing decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design stimuli so that only the intended manipulations (score, qualitative evaluation, ethnicity when relevant) vary across conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Measure stereotype alignment explicitly
rubrics_metrics.description: Operationalize and manipulate whether algorithmic/human advice aligns with group stereotypes (e.g., ethnicity of teacher) to test selective adherence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Restrict selective adherence analysis to participants for whom the group manipulation is meaningful (the study excluded non-Dutch descent participants from H2/H3 analysis) and predefine subgroup analyses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interaction tests to evaluate moderation hypotheses
rubrics_metrics.description: Test whether adherence differences depend jointly on advice source and stereotype alignment (i.e., interaction between algorithmic vs human advice and target's group).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examine interaction terms and conduct robustness checks; be cautious interpreting non-significant interactions (follow statistical best-practices).

rubrics_metrics.name: Theoretical integration from multiple literatures
rubrics_metrics.description: Ground hypotheses in both social psychology (automation bias, algorithm appreciation) and public administration literatures (motivated reasoning, bureaucratic discrimination) to generate competing predictions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use cross-disciplinary theory to motivate experimental contrasts and interpret heterogeneous results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Realistic numeric scale design
rubrics_metrics.description: Design the numeric predictive scale to mirror commonly used risk scores (example: 1–10 scale resembling COMPAS).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Selecting a familiar or realistic numeric range can increase ecological validity and comparability to prior studies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency, documentation, and supplementary materials
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide appendices, supplementary tables, preregistration links, details of manipulations, sample characteristics, and reference materials to allow replication and scrutiny.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report recruitment source, data exclusions, demographic breakdowns, and provide supplementary analyses and robustness checks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discuss normative and policy implications
rubrics_metrics.description: After empirical testing, articulate implications for public-sector decision making, accountability, bureaucratic legitimacy, and impacts on vulnerable groups.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Connect empirical findings to broader debates about algorithmic governance and suggest directions for policy or institutional safeguards when biases are present.
